title: In An-Nadwah (Council) House The Parliament of Quraish

topics.title: In An-Nadwah (Council) House The Parliament of Quraish

paragraphs.text: The polytheists were paralysed by the carefully planned and speedy movement of Muhammad's followers towards their new abode in Madinah. They were caught in unprecedented anxiety and got deeply worried over their whole pagan and economic entity. They already experienced Muhammad (Peace be upon him) as an influential leader, and his followers as determined and always ready to sacrifice all they had for the sake of the Messenger of Allah (Peace be upon him). Al-Aws and Al-Khazraj tribes, the would-be hosts of the Makkan Muslims, were known in Arabia for their might in war and their judicious approach in peace.

Madinah itself, the prospective headquarters of the ever-growing Islamic Call, enjoyed the most serious strategic position. It commanded the commercial routes leading to Makkah, whose people used to deal in about a quarter of a million gold dinar-worth of commodities every year. Security of the caravan routes was crucial for the perpetuity of prosperous economic life. With all those factors borne in mind, the polytheists felt they were in the grip of a serious threat, and began to seek the most effective method to avert this imminent danger.

They convened a meeting on Thursday, 26th Safar, the year fourteen of Prophethood / 12th September 622 A.D., i.e. two and a half months after the Great 'Aqabah Pledge. On that day, 'the Parliament of Makkah' held the most serious meeting ever, with one item on the agenda: how to take effective measures to stop that tidal wave. Delegates representing all the Quraishite tribes attended, the most significant of whom were: Abu Jahl bin Hisham (Bani Makhzum); Jubair bin Mut'im, Tuaima bin 'Adi and Al-Harith bin 'Amir (Bani Naufal); Shaibah and 'Utbah, the two sons of Rabi'a, and Abu Sufyan bin Harb (Bani 'Abd Shams); An-Nadr bin Al-Harith (Bani 'Abd Ad-Dar); Abul Bukhtary bin Hisham, Zama'a bin Al-Aswad and Hakeem bin Hizam (Bani Asad); Nabih and Munbih, the two sons of Al-Hajjaj (Bani Sahm); and Omaiyah bin Khalaf (Bani Jumah).

On their way to An-Nadwah House, Iblis (Satan) in the guise of a venerable elderly man stood at the door, introduced himself as a man from Najd curious to attend the meeting, and was readily admitted. There was a lengthy debate. Expulsion from Makkah was proposed but turned down, on the grounds that his sweet, heart-touching words could entice the other Arabs to attack Quraish in their own city. Imprisonment for life was also debated but refused, for fear that his followers might increase, overpower them and release him by force.

At this point, the arch-criminal of Makkah, Abu Jahl bin Hisham, suggested that they assassinate him. But assassination by one man would expose him and his family to the vengeance of blood. The difficulty was solved by Abu Jahl himself, who suggested that a band of young men, one from each tribe, should strike Muhammad (Peace be upon him) simultaneously with their swords, so that the blood-money would be spread over all the tribes and could not be exacted, and his people would have to seek a settlement based on reason. The sinful proposal was unanimously accepted, and the representatives broke up the meeting with full determination for immediate implementation.

topics.topicSummary: Alarmed by the swift migration of the Muslims and the strategic threat of Madinah (which commanded their vital trade routes), Quraish convened their council, 'An-Nadwah House', on 26th Safar of year 14. With Iblis present in disguise as a Najdi elder, they debated and rejected expelling or imprisoning the Prophet ﷺ, until Abu Jahl proposed the fatal plan: a young man from every tribe would strike him together, so the blood-guilt would be shared and no single clan could be held to account.
keyPoints: Quraish were alarmed by the swift migration and the strategic threat posed by Madinah
Madinah commanded the caravan routes vital to Makkah's quarter-million-dinar annual trade
They convened the council of An-Nadwah House on 26th Safar of year 14 (12 Sept 622 A.D.)
Iblis attended in the guise of a venerable elder from Najd
They rejected expelling the Prophet ﷺ (fearing he would win over other Arabs) and imprisoning him (fearing his followers)
Abu Jahl proposed that a young man from each tribe strike him together, so the blood-guilt would be shared
The murder plot was unanimously accepted for immediate implementation

quiz.question: What was the single item on the agenda of the An-Nadwah House meeting?
options: How to stop the tidal wave of Islam (and deal with the Prophet ﷺ)
How to make peace with the Aws and Khazraj
quiz.answer: How to stop the tidal wave of Islam (and deal with the Prophet ﷺ)

quiz.question: In what guise did Iblis attend the meeting?
options: A venerable elderly man from Najd
quiz.answer: A venerable elderly man from Najd

quiz.question: What was Abu Jahl's final plan that the council accepted?
options: To expel the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah
To have a young man from each tribe strike him together so the blood-guilt would be shared
quiz.answer: To have a young man from each tribe strike him together so the blood-guilt would be shared
